calls.head: Strength vs. strength
calls.body: The Bruins are one of the league’s best for chance quality, but the Kings are one of the best at preventing dangerous shots. We think the Bruins still get theirs.
calls.call: The Bruins’ chances are more dangerous than the league average (a 6.3% chance of scoring on the average shot) against the Kings.

calls.head: A shadow job for Mittelstadt, Lindholm and Khusnutdinov
calls.body: At home, the Bruins keep sending Lindholm’s line (Mittelstadt, Lindholm and Khusnutdinov) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Marco Sturm has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Kings’ first line is Turcotte, Laferriere and Kempe.
calls.call: The Bruins’ L2 (Mittelstadt, Lindholm and Khusnutdinov) spends at least 49% of its 5-on-5 time against the Kings’ first line, against about 37% with no line matching.
calls.nums: At home: 61% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 37% with no line matching

The ring is the call: halfway from what it would get with no line matching (the tick) to its home habit (the dotted mark), since part of any habit is luck. Reaching the ring holds the call; past the tick is partly; otherwise it didn’t happen.

calls.title: Mittelstadt, Lindholm and Khusnutdinov barely saw the Kings’ first line
calls.plain: Boston sent Mittelstadt, Lindholm and Khusnutdinov out against the Kings’ first line no more than they would with no line matching. Instead, Sturm sent them out against Fiala, Byfield and Zuccarello (2:57 of 8:04 at 5-on-5).
calls.said: Marco Sturm would send Mittelstadt, Lindholm and Khusnutdinov out against the Kings’ first line again

calls.head: The Kings hound the puck, the Bruins sit back
calls.body: On forecheck pressure, Los Angeles is one of the league’s best, but Boston is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Expect the Kings to win more pucks back deep in the Bruins’ end.
calls.call: The Kings put more forecheck pressure on than the Bruins.

surprises.head: Boston shut down Los Angeles’s power play
surprises.body: Los Angeles’s power play created 0.9 expected goals per 60, against their usual 7.7 and a league average of 7.8. A team strays this far about once every 80 games.

surprises.head: Boston couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Boston’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 4.0% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.8% (about 6.4% against Los Angeles) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 45 games.

story.head: Kuemper slams the door on the Bruins
paras: Mats Zuccarello opened the scoring for the Kings late in the first. Michael DiPietro stopped Quinton Byfield on a penalty shot early in the second, but that’s where Boston’s luck ran out. Andre Lee pushed the lead to 2-0 late in the period. Darcy Kuemper stopped Morgan Geekie on a penalty shot midway through the third. Erik Gustafsson added an empty-net goal with just over three minutes left to make it 3-0.
The Bruins had a little more of the play, but the Kings made their chances count. The Kings moved to 6-11-2, seventh in the Pacific, while the Bruins dropped to 13-7-1, fourth in the Atlantic.

items.text: The Kings won for the first time in five games.
The Bruins are on a three-game losing streak.
The season series is even at 1-1.
None of the preview’s three calls held.
